text:
zoe: Quick check: onboarding spectral-anchor-embed (512d). After ONNX int4-perchannel conversion I'm seeing kmeans inertia spike and KNN recall@10 drop ~3.2% on the forum-holdout slice. Weirdly silhouette score also drops while L2 norms preserve. Anyone seen centroid "leak" like this with low-bit quant? 

anand: which eval and command?

zoe: forum-holdout-2m, weekly split. Ran:

```
python eval_embeddings.py \n  --model spectral-anchor-embed-v1 \n  --quant onnx-int4_perchannel \n  --dataset forum-holdout-2m \n  --split weekly \n  --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,kmeans_inertia,centroid_leak
```

jess: centroid_leak metric? new to me. What's the definition?

zoe: it's simple: fraction of cluster mass that migrates to a different centroid when comparing fp16->quantized cluster assignments (kmeans k=100). Basically tracks points that flip cluster membership and how far they move.

ravi: numbers?

zoe: paste from the run:
- fp16: @1=0.498, @5=0.693, @10=0.764, silhouette=0.198, inertia=1.12e5, centroid_leak=0.042
- int4: @1=0.478, @5=0.655, @10=0.732, silhouette=0.157, inertia=1.41e5, centroid_leak=0.101

anand: big jump in centroid_leak. Did you use global centroids from fp16 to compare or recompute kmeans per-precision?

zoe: recomputed kmeans separately for each precision and then matched centroids by nearest-pair. Could also try assigning quant vectors to fp16 centroids to isolate embedding shifts vs clustering instability.

jess: try assigning quant -> fp16 centroids (one-way) to see if the quant vectors move relative to fp16 centers. That isolates embedding bias from kmeans randomness.

mlbot: eval-bot: queued job 33321 (assign-quant-to-fp16-centroids) for zoe.

zoe: good idea. Also inspected per-dim histograms: int4 shows heavy clipping on dims 48..72. Per-channel quant seems better but still clips some tail mass.

ravi: two experiments to try: (1) int4-perchannel calibration with a larger stratified sample (50k) and (2) compute PCA on fp16 centroids and measure projection of quant bias onto top 3 PCs. If bias concentrates in few PCs, a low-rank debias at index time might help.

anand: also check HNSW sensitivity. Re-indexing with ef_construction=300 and ef_search=200 can recover part of recall loss when perturbations are small.

zoe: ran the assignment test (quant vectors -> fp16 centroids): centroid_leak (one-way) drops from 0.101 -> 0.063, inertia gap narrows. So some instability is from kmeans re-running.

jess: good sign. What's the PCA projection show?

zoe: PCA on fp16 centroids: PC1..PC3 explain 48%, 11%, 6% variance. Quant bias projected ~0.86 onto PC1 for many weeks (i.e., strong alignment). Removing a small projection (~0.02 L2) along PC1 from quant vectors reduces centroid_leak one-way by ~0.015 and improves rec@10 ~+0.008.

ravi: promising. But be careful — removing an axis could harm some classes. Validate class-level recall and per-week stability.

zoe: did per-class checks: 4/6 major categories improved, 2 (very small classes) dropped slightly. Might be acceptable if weighted by traffic.

anand: include an opt-in debias step at index-time and add a per-class guardrail script that rejects debias if class recall degrades > 0.5%.

mlbot: job 33321 completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/spectral-anchor/v1/onboard/4832107777/job-33321/

zoe: interim: int4-perchannel calibration (50k) + pc1-debias + ef_construction=300 + ef_search=200 recovered rec@10 to 0.757 (fp16 baseline 0.764). Centroid_leak one-way down to 0.038. Latency impact: index-time debias negligible, query-time ef increase raised median latency from 12ms -> 18ms (within SLO for non-SLA tier).

jess: sounds reasonable. Add to onboarding checklist: 1) int4-perchannel calibrate on 50k stratified sample, 2) assignment test (quant->fp16 centroids), 3) PCA axis check + opt-in index-time debias, 4) HNSW ef tuning guidance, 5) per-class guardrail checks.

ravi: one more thought: try small temperature scaling on similarities or learned per-dim scaling (diagonal affine) instead of axis removal; may generalize better.

zoe: scheduling diag runs for temp-scaling and per-dim affine. Will post final 2-week rolling results and open PR for onboarding docs if stable. Thanks for the tips.

infra-bot: infra note: quant runs used staging-gpu-c (cuda 12.2, onnxrt 1.16) similar to prod. Keep env flags consistent when moving to prod.

zoe: noted. I'll attach artifacts and scripts to the onboarding ticket.
